chunks: When Moses arrived at the appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said: "O Lord, reveal Yourself to me that I may behold You." "You cannot behold Me," He said. "But look at the mountain: If it remains firm in its place you may then behold Me." But when his Lord appeared on the mountain in His effulgence, it crumbled to a heap of dust, and Moses fell unconscious. When he came to, he said: "All glory to You. I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first to believe."
ai.seo_question: What was the sign God gave Moses to demonstrate His presence, and what happened to the mountain?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the fundamental distinction between God's essence (Dhat) and His attributes, illustrating that while God is unseen in His essence, His signs (Ayat) are manifest in creation. The mountain's crumbling signifies the inability of created matter to withstand the divine effulgence, while Moses' declaration of being the 'first of the believers' is interpreted by scholars like Al-Tabarsi as either his unique status among his people or his affirmation of faith after the initial doubt of the vision request. This event serves as a cornerstone for understanding the concept of 'Tajalli' (divine self-disclosure) in Islamic theology.
